name: Korean peninsula (North Korean missile tests and Russia alliance)
started: 1953-07-27 (armistice); current phase of intensified missile testing and military alliance with Russia since 2024
summary: There is no fighting across the DMZ, but North Korea is testing missiles at more than double its 2025 pace, including a new hypersonic-glide variant and missiles flying over 900 km, while its troops and workers support Russia's war against Ukraine. Closer ties with both Moscow and Beijing in 2026 have reduced its isolation.

sides.name: North Korea
members: KPA special operations forces deployed to Russia
backers: Russia (mutual defence treaty ratified Nov 2024; military technology and revenue)
leaders: Kim Jong Un (General Secretary, reappointed 22 Feb 2026; chairman of the State Affairs Commission)
sides.strength: 12,000 to 15,000 troops sent to Russia (Wikipedia compilation of US, South Korean and Ukrainian estimates).

sides.name: South Korea, United States and Japan
members: Republic of Korea Armed Forces (Joint Chiefs of Staff)
Japan Ministry of Defense (tracking and information-sharing)

background: The Korean War ended in an armistice in 1953, not a peace treaty. Since 2024 North Korea has declared the South a separate hostile state, signed a mutual defence treaty with Russia and sent troops to help expel Ukrainian forces from Russia's Kursk region, receiving revenue estimated at over $10 billion and access to Russian military technology in return.

This matters because combat experience, Russian help and frequent testing are improving the North's short-range and hypersonic missiles, which are designed to defeat South Korean, Japanese and US missile defences.
year: North Korea tested two hypersonic missiles on 22 October 2025 and a ballistic missile on 7 November 2025. In 2026 it fired several ballistic missiles on 4 January, two on 27 January and about ten from the Sunan area on 14 March. The 9th Party Congress (19-25 February) reappointed Kim Jong Un. It tested the Hwasongpho-11 Ka tactical missile on 8 April, five Hwasongpho-11 Ra on 19 April (reported with cluster munitions), close-range missiles into the Yellow Sea on 25 May, an SRBM on 6 August and a missile from Wonsan on 12 August. Xi Jinping visited Pyongyang on 8 June, the first Xi-Kim meeting in seven years, and a road bridge to Russia opened on 8 September. On 20 September it tested what it called a Hwasong-11Ma-1 variant with a hypersonic glide vehicle warhead. Ukraine transferred two captured North Korean soldiers to South Korea on 23 September. On 3 October a missile flew more than 700 km from the Wonsan area, and on 12 October two missiles were fired from near Pyongyang, one flying over 910 km, after a South Korean hypersonic test. Seoul also reported a DMZ landmine explosion that injured South Korean soldiers in early October.
situation: As of late October 2026 the peninsula is tense but without armed clashes. North Korea is in an intensive testing cycle: on 29 October it fired about 10 short-range ballistic missiles from near Wonsan into the sea, after South Korea's JCS had counted the 3 October launch as the 16th ballistic launch of the year (Japan counts launch events differently). Relations are strained by a September DMZ landmine blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers, which a South Korea-UN investigation blamed on North Korea and Pyongyang denies, and by US-South Korean stealth-jet drills at Kunsan running into November. Trump has suggested he might meet Kim Jong Un this year.
technical: 20 Sep 2026: range about 440 km, apogee about 60 km; North Korea said it was a new Hwasong-11Ma-1 variant with a hypersonic glide vehicle warhead (Militarnyi, citing Japan MoD).

12 Oct 2026: two ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area (~9:20 am); one flew about 220 km with a 20 km apogee, the other 910+ km with a 70 km apogee, a depressed trajectory consistent with evading defences (Militarnyi; Korea Times).
3 Oct 2026: one ballistic missile from the Wonsan area (Sangum-ri, Anbyon County per Wikipedia), 700+ km; Kim Yo Jong called it an intermediate-range missile (Daily Pioneer; Wikipedia).
19 Apr 2026: five Hwasongpho-11 Ra surface-to-surface tactical ballistic missiles; reported with cluster munition warhead (Wikipedia).
8 Apr 2026: Hwasongpho-11 Ka tactical missile during a week of weapons tests (Wikipedia).
14 Mar 2026: about 10 ballistic missiles from the Sunan launch site (Wikipedia).
Testing tempo: Japan counted at least 11 launch events and 18+ missiles in 2026 by 12 Oct, more than double 2025's launches and about triple its missile count (Militarnyi).
Troops in Russia: 12,000 to 15,000 (about 500 officers, three generals), mostly special operations forces; still present in Kursk border areas in Feb 2026 per Ukraine's DIU (Wikipedia).

Arms to Russia: shells estimated at 4 million (Open Source Centre, to Apr 2025) to 12 million (CFR, to Jul 2025); 148 Hwasong-11 type missiles by early 2025 (Ukrainian intelligence); about 50 Koksan M-1989 SPGs and 20 M-1991 MRLs (Wikipedia).
Revenue: over $10 billion from arms sales to Russia mid-2023 to end-2025, against a GDP of about $27 billion (Wikipedia).
Russia-North Korea road bridge over the Tumen (Rason-Khasan) opened 8 Sep 2026; Sinuiju-Dandong Yalu road bridge inaugurated 14 Oct 2026 (Wikipedia).
casualties: No inter-Korean combat deaths found for the window. South Korean soldiers were injured by a DMZ landmine in early Oct 2026 (Daily Pioneer). North Korean losses in Russia were estimated at 300 killed and 2,700 wounded (South Korea's NIS) to about 1,000 killed (Western officials) as of Jan 2025; no updated figure retrieved.

timeline.event: Several ballistic missiles fired toward the East Sea.
About 10 ballistic missiles fired from Sunan.
Five Hwasongpho-11 Ra tactical missiles fired.
Hwasong-11Ma-1 hypersonic glide vehicle variant tested.
Ukraine transfers two captured North Korean soldiers to South Korea.
Missile from Wonsan area flies 700+ km.
Two missiles from near Pyongyang, one 910+ km.
About 10 short-range ballistic missiles fired from near Wonsan (South Korean JCS).

outlook: Watch for an ICBM flight test (none confirmed for 2026 in sources retrieved), a nuclear test, more hypersonic glide tests, and any new deployment to Russia or Ukraine. China's renewed embrace and Russian support reduce the leverage of sanctions.

battles.name: North Korean two-missile launch near Pyongyang
sides: South Korea, United States and Japan (tracking)
battles.outcome: Two ballistic missiles fell outside Japan's EEZ; one flew about 220 km, the other 910+ km.
battles.forces: Two ballistic missiles; apogees about 20 km and 70 km.
battles.significance: Low apogees over long range suggest manoeuvring or depressed-trajectory systems built to beat missile defences; launched right after a South Korean hypersonic test.

battles.name: North Korean launch from the Wonsan area
battles.place: Wonsan area (Sangum-ri, Anbyon County), Kangwon Province, North Korea
sides: South Korea, United States and Japan (tracking)
battles.outcome: One ballistic missile flew more than 700 km into the East Sea; Kim Yo Jong described it as an intermediate-range missile.
battles.significance: South Korea's JCS counted it as the 16th ballistic launch of 2026; it came amid a DMZ landmine incident that injured South Korean soldiers.

battles.name: North Korean ten-missile salvo from Sunan
sides: South Korea, United States and Japan (tracking)
battles.outcome: About 10 ballistic missiles fired into the Sea of Japan.
battles.forces: Ballistic missiles (types not specified in sources retrieved).
battles.significance: One of the largest single salvos of the year, practising mass launches meant to saturate missile defences.
